page: Amazon Web Services c4.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the Xen hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2666 v3 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 dedicated physical core with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 2.9 GHz. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 1.88 GB of RAM per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and 25 MB of L3 cache. It supports hardware-assisted features such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX), AES cryptography, and Fused Multiply-Add (FMA) instructions.

In benchmark testing, the c4.large demonstrates moderate single-core performance but limited multi-core scaling. The stress-ng single-core CPU test scores 1478.68, placing it in the average range, while the multi-core CPU performance drops to 1945.19, which is in the bottom 10%. Single-threaded compression tasks perform relatively well, with gzip compression reaching 24.27 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression achieving 9.16 GB/sec. However, memory bandwidth is a bottleneck; read-only large block bandwidth is measured at 13.03 GB/sec, and write large block bandwidth is 11.47 GB/sec, both falling into the bottom 10%. Geekbench testing reflects this trend, with a single-core score of 1133.0 and a multi-core score of 1368.0.

This instance does not include local NVMe or SSD storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data. Network connectivity is limited to a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included. Given the dedicated CPU allocation but low memory capacity and weak multi-core performance, the c4.large is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded compute tasks, basic web serving, or small-scale utility workloads that require dedicated CPU resources but do not demand high memory bandwidth or intensive parallel processing.
